# ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.22 acceptance (c) — the DECLARED no-dump roster.
# A corpus file that produces no rule-outcome dump is a file the parse-cost measurement does not
# cover. Before this roster existed the row was folded into an integer, the integer was printed,
# and the run continued — which is how `.20` slice 1 published "zero no-dump rows" and
# "16 336/16 336 agree" while ONE file was silently absent, and that one file measurably moved
# 5 of the 192 PINNED sample rows (`.21` slice 1 RESULT 5).
# ⛔ EVERY no-dump file must appear here WITH THE LEAF THAT OWNS FIXING IT, or the run REFUSES
# (`adjudicate_nodump`, exit 2). This is a declaration of a known defect, never a waiver: the row
# exists so the drop is visible in the artifact, attributable to an owner, and detectable when it
# changes. A NEW drop is not in this file and therefore stops the measurement.
# ⛔ DO NOT "fix" a row here by raising PER_FILE_TIMEOUT_S. `.22` measured the blow-up as
# EXPONENTIAL — the transactional coverage stack grows ×4.14 per else-if arm while the parse
# itself grows linearly (+19 295 rule entries per arm) — so no timeout is large enough and every
# timeout is arbitrary. The fix is in the engine, not in the clock.
# ⛔ THE ROSTER KEYS ON `path`, NOT ON `reason`, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The SAME file surfaces
# as `timeout` when measured serially and as `empty-dump` under `-j8`, because the OS reclaims
# the 13.7 GB process before the 120 s timeout expires. Both are the same defect; gating on the
# reason would make the check flaky on exactly the file it exists for. The observed reason is
# PRINTED on every run so a change in symptom is still visible.
# 4 tab-separated fields:  path <TAB> reason <TAB> owning-leaf <TAB> note

column4: Bare parse 0.108 s and the TOOLBOX 3.4 entry dump 0.056 s / 200 975 entries / accepted=True; the TOOLBOX 3.5 outcome dump never terminates. Same PROTOCOL graph in both, so the defect is the transactional coverage stack alone. Root cause: memoized_call stores coverage_stack[checkpoint..].to_vec() per memo entry and replays it with extend_from_slice on every hit, which materialises the shared parse DAG as a TREE. Measured growth on the else-if ladder: entries LINEAR (+19 295/arm), coverage stack EXPONENTIAL (x4.14/arm) reaching 353 005 042 slots at 7 arms; this file has 10, extrapolating to ~93 GB. /usr/bin/sample: _platform_memmove is 4302 of 4314 samples = 99.7 % of CPU.
